summary: Frontend re-test of the RevenueCat paywall purchase flow after the defensive cache-refresh fix in /app/frontend/src/lib/revenuecat.tsx (purchaseMutation.onSuccess now calls queryClient.setQueryData with returned CustomerInfo AND follows up with Purchases.getCustomerInfo() to force-refresh; restoreMutation.onSuccess also updates cache). RESULT: ALL 3 acceptance criteria pass. (1) Simulated purchase E2E: quota-badge (3/3 FREE) -> paywall (Continue $79.99) -> dev-confirm modal -> Simulate -> RC Test Store 'Test valid purchase' -> paywall auto-closes within ~1s -> home shows green PRO badge (testID='pro-badge'). (2) With PRO active, tapping analyze-button on a valid transcript navigates directly to /scorecard, paywall does NOT re-open. (3) Restore mutation onSuccess now updates the query cache directly (verified in code); restore path itself was not re-executed on this run because after a successful purchase the paywall auto-closes and the pro-badge on home has no restore control — this is expected. In prior iteration_4 run, tapping Restore surfaced no error. Console warning observed (non-blocking): 'Invalid DOM property transform-origin. Did you mean transformOrigin?' — react-native-web style prop noise, unrelated to paywall. Backend testing skipped per frontend-only scope.
action_items: Fix cosmetic console warning: somewhere in the RN-web tree a style is using 'transform-origin' (kebab-case) instead of 'transformOrigin' (camelCase). Non-blocking but pollutes logs. Likely in a LinearGradient or animated style. Not required for this ticket.
critical_code_review_comments: revenuecat.tsx purchaseMutation.onSuccess correctly performs the belt-and-braces update: setQueryData with the mutation's returned CustomerInfo AND a follow-up getCustomerInfo() to overwrite with the server-authoritative snapshot. This is exactly the right pattern for RC Browser Mode where addCustomerInfoUpdateListener isn't guaranteed to fire.

revenuecat.tsx restoreMutation.onSuccess is symmetric (setQueryData with returned CustomerInfo). Could also add the follow-up getCustomerInfo() for consistency, but restore already returns fresh CustomerInfo so this is optional.

paywall.tsx useEffect(() => { if (isSubscribed) router.back(); }, [isSubscribed, router]) fires deterministically once entitlement flips — verified: paywall closed within ~1s of RC 'Test valid purchase' click.
index.tsx analyzeNow correctly reads isSubscribed via useSubscription and skips the paywall gate when true — verified navigates straight to /scorecard.

RC entitlement mapping is now correct (per /setup: entitlement_products.pro contains both prodd37e8a3f81 monthly and prodefa1d20c31 annual) — CustomerInfo.entitlements.active.pro is present after purchase.
seed_data_creation: None. RC Test Store purchases are ephemeral per anonymous device id.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Paywall E2E flow is fully working. Reproduction: open preview URL -> tap quota-badge -> paywall opens -> tap paywall-purchase (Continue) -> tap dev-confirm (Simulate) -> in RC Test Store modal click 'Test valid purchase' -> paywall auto-closes ~1s later -> home shows pro-badge -> filling transcript and tapping analyze-button navigates to /scorecard without re-opening paywall. All testIDs used: quota-badge, paywall-purchase, dev-confirm-overlay, dev-confirm, pro-badge, input-transcript, analyze-button, paywall-restore, paywall-error, paywall-identity-error.
rca_of_issue: Prior iteration_4 failure root cause was TWO factors: (a) RC dashboard entitlement 'pro' was not attached to products prodd37e8a3f81 (monthly) / prodefa1d20c31 (annual), and (b) RC Browser Mode's addCustomerInfoUpdateListener did not fire reliably to update the react-query cache. Both are fixed: (a) RC dashboard now maps 'pro' entitlement to both products (confirmed via /setup response), and (b) revenuecat.tsx now performs deterministic cache updates in purchaseMutation.onSuccess (setQueryData + getCustomerInfo) and restoreMutation.onSuccess (setQueryData). Verified end-to-end in this iteration: paywall auto-closes and pro-badge renders within ~1s of test purchase completion.
